stories.headline: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.title: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.summary: Minister K.Vignesh inspects monsoon preparedness in some of the most flood prone areas in the southern part of the city
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Excise and Prohibition Minister K. Vignesh on Monday reviewed the monsoon preparedness work in some of the most flood-prone areas in the southern parts of the city and ordered officials to expedite work on relief centres at 27 locations to help residents during the Northeast monsoon.
He also directed officials to complete work in three days.

Owing to the risk of heavy flooding in the southern parts of the city, the Minister directed the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) to expedite work on water supply, toilet facilities, power, and food for residents at relief centres.

The Minister ordered officials to prepare food for residents of flood-prone areas by facilitating the supply of food from 21 Amma Canteens in Perungudi, 17 Amma canteens in Sholinganallur, and six community kitchens.
The Minister advised.
THE GCC to appoint nodal officers to prepare the food for distribution.
He also directed officials to coordinate with fire and rescue services to catch snakes in flood-prone residential areas in the two zones during the monsoon.
In Sholinganallur zone, work on 95.7 km of drains has been completed.
Work on 13.385 km of drains is under way.
In Perungudi, 145.27 km of drains out of 154.19 km has been completed.
Work on 73 metres of drains in nine stretches is under way.
The Minister directed officials to expedite the work.

stories.title: Punjab: Akali Dal to announce election manifesto on Nov 1
stories.summary: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: wire echo (ians) -> no independent boost
article_sentences: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.

Chandigarh: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.
The yatra, which will be led by party President Sukhbir Badal, will be conducted in three phases, with the first phase being held from November 10 to 22.
The second phase will be launched from Sri Anandpur Sahib and the third one from Sri Akal Takht Sahib.

Disclosing this after the culmination of a series of meetings with the party’s Scheduled Caste, Backward Class and Youth wing, which were presided over by Badal, senior leader Daljit Cheema said the party President took first-hand feedback on issues to be included in the party’s election manifesto as well as focusing on improving the party organisation.
He said the feedback received from the different party wings would be taken up for consideration in the next meeting of the party’s election manifesto committee on October 24.
“The manifesto will be released on November 1,” he added.

Badal told the media that the arrest of Amardeep Grewal, the brother-in-law of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s wife Gurpreet Kaur, would bring the corruption being done in the Chief Minister’s residence before the people.
“Be it Bhagwant Mann or his Arvind Kejriwal, the central agencies are closing in on all of them.
All of them will be booked and will face the consequences of their corrupt acts.”
Badal said the Chief Minister was directly responsible for the murder of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota.
He said instead of ending the drug menace, the Yudh Nasheyan Virudh campaign of the AAP government was resulting in the killing of anti-drug activists and whistleblowers.

stories.headline: CJI Surya Kant to visit Ladakh tomorrow to inaugurate Ladakh Bench of High Court
stories.title: CJI Surya Kant to visit Ladakh tomorrow to inaugurate Ladakh Bench of High Court
stories.summary: Ladakh, Oct 17: The Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kant, will visit Ladakh on Sunday to inaugurate the newly constituted Ladakh bench of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra said at a press conference today. He said the CJI will be accompanied by four Supreme Court judges, the chief justice of the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court, and other high court judges. The attorney general of India will also attend the event, he said. “It is a very big thing. Frankly speaking in recent times, if you scan the history of the High Courts in India, I don't think that in the last 40 years any sitting bench has been set up in this fashion for any other High Court. The only example which comes to my mind is maybe that of the North Eastern States, where the Guwahati High Court, had benches in Arunachal Pradesh, where I have worked,” he said. “Justice coming closer to the people is a very big thing,” the CS said. “Otherwise, anyone who was aggrieved and wanted to file a writ petition would have to go to Srinagar or Jammu. I think the fact that this is now possible here in Ladakh is an extremely positive development,” he added. He said the bench was established within two months and was not among the demands raised during negotiations, describing it as a unilateral initiative by the Centre. Negotiations are currently underway between Ladakhi political leaders and the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Ladakhi leaders are seeking a Union Territory with a legislature and constitutional safeguards under Article 371. “The Government of India fully understands how difficult this terrain is, the challenging circumstances in which people live here and how crucial it is to ensure that justice is accessible closer to their doorstep,” Kundra said.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
stories.title: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved a new industrial policy that outlines a ten-year roadmap for developing a clean, knowledge-based industrial economy in the Capital, with a focus on high-value, non-polluting sectors, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said on Wednesday.

The Industrial Policy, 2026, approved in a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, also allocated Rs 1,000 crore under Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana for five years to promote new industries and create jobs, said the statement.

Under the new policy, special incentives will be given for 10 priority sectors, including Information Technology (IT), global capability centres, data centres, healthcare, research and modern manufacturing, as per the CMO.
“Women-led micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will receive additional support for business modernisation and expansion.
Employers hiring women will receive higher incentives for each woman recruited.
Women and young people will also receive special attention under skill development programmes.
These provisions aim to expand business and employment opportunities for women entrepreneurs and employees,” said the statement.
Ms. Gupta said the policy focuses on making better use of the Capital’s economic potential by encouraging advanced technology, research, specialised services and high-value-added industries.

“Over the next 10 years, it aims to create an investment-friendly environment, provide necessary support to entrepreneurs, promote women-led enterprises and generate new employment opportunities for young people.
It will also seek to steer Delhi’s industrial economy towards a more modern, cleaner and knowledge-based model,” she said.

Ms. Gupta said that considering the needs of different sectors, tailored incentives would be provided for capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new hiring, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy conservation and skill development.
The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction, she added.

stories.headline: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.title: Supreme Court mandates insurance on offline railway tickets from October 27
stories.summary: ‘At present, only persons purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has issued a mandatory directive that tickets sold across counters at every railway station nationwide must include travel insurance coverage identical to online bookings.
A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed the railway authorities to put the order into effect from October 27, 2026.
The order explicitly warned that failure to implement this mechanism would place direct liability squarely on the Railway Board.
“At present, only people purchasing tickets online are provided the benefit of insurance coverage upon payment of a nominal additional amount.

The court had granted sufficient time to the authorities to devise a mechanism extending such coverage to persons belonging to the lowest strata of society, who, in most cases, purchase their tickets at the railway reservation counters while undertaking journeys by train,” the court observed, pointing out that the railway had made no progress on providing insurance cover to all passengers.
The direction was based on a writ petition filed in the aftermath of the June 2023 Odisha train accident.
The petition initially focused on an independent probe into the accident and the implementation of safety systems like Kavach.

However, the court widened the scope of the case to include various passenger and infrastructural aspects of rail travel, including the lack of insurance for economically disadvantaged passengers who purchase tickets over the counter at stations.

The court, in its order dated October 6, recorded its “utter disappointment and displeasure at the conduct of the officers of the Ministry of Railways in such a serious matter concerning the safety of the common man”.
“The Railways have been representing before this court that all necessary steps are being taken in this regard.
However, it appears that such assurances have remained largely on paper and that no substantial change has taken place on the ground,” the court noted.
In a scathing order, the bench said even the budgetary provisions for the targeted areas relating to the safety of the common man and the prevention of untoward incidents had not been fully utilised.

stories.headline: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
stories.title: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
stories.summary: The Bench also quashed a U.P. Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Abhishek Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) made absolute the interim protection granted to independent journalist Abhishek Upadhyay from coercive action in a road rage case, as well as any subsequent First Information Reports.
Mr. Upadhyay had authored investigative online stories of the alleged misappropriation and theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple.
A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi also quashed an Uttar Pradesh.
Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Mr. Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident.
The court found the police version that the data was sought to trace/arrest the petitioner “somewhat in contradiction” with the contents of its notice to the platform.
The court termed the notice an “overkill”, and said any information received by the police pursuant to the notice would not be used against the journalist.
The “arrest of the petitioner (Mr. Upadhyay) shall remain stayed till further notice,” the court said.
It made absolute its interim orders of August 25 and September 7, which had protected him from arrest and directed him to cooperate with the investigation, respectively.
The copy of the road rage FIR had been supplied to the petitioner, the court noted.
The Bench ordered that Mr. Upadhyay could challenge the road rage FIR on any grounds.
The apex court has not commented on the merits of the case.

The court allowed Mr. Upadhyay, who said the road rage case was “staged”, to counter his online reports about the temple, and the liberty to file a separate petition seeking guidelines to protect digital privacy and journalistic freedoms.

stories.headline: Delhi protests: Metro was ‘fully functional’, 32 lakh rode trains on October 10: DMRC tells Supreme Court
stories.title: Delhi protests: Metro was ‘fully functional’, 32 lakh rode trains on October 10: DMRC tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: Admits commuter traffic ‘slightly lower’ than usual second-Saturday count of 58 lakh, says protests may have dampened people’s willingness to travel
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) and its chairperson filed separate affidavits in the Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026), stating that the Metro network remained “fully functional” on October 10, recording 32 lakh passengers.
“There was zero reduction in the total volume of metro operation or the number of train trips,” the DMRC said.

Though the DMRC admitted that commuter traffic was “slightly lower” than the typical 58 lakh passengers on a “normal” second Saturday, it attributed the drop to public caution amid protests rather than administrative paralysis.
It said ordinary citizens were “compelled to forgo their usual day-to-day activities” on October 10.
The day saw heavy security crackdowns in the capital against demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Petitioners like CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi had argued that widespread barricading and station closures violated an October 9 Supreme Court order mandating proportionate movement restrictions.
Defending its actions, the DMRC said entry and exit regulations were limited to 45 of the network’s 303 stations on October 10.
Though the initial count of the number of stations to be closed on October 10 was 57, it was scaled down to 45, accounting for about 15% of the network.
“Over 85% of the network (258 stations) remained fully operational, accessible, and functional for commuters,” the DMRC stated.

Crucially, of the 45 stations where entry and exit gates were regulated, 14 key interchange stations (including major transit hubs such as Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Central Secretariat, Mandi House, Hauz Khas, Dilli Haat-INA, and Netaji Subhash Place) continued to provide full and uninterrupted line-interchange facilities for commuters.
Commuters entering the city as well as inside the city were able to change transit corridors seamlessly without disruption, the affidavit said.
“For the limited stations where passenger gates were regulated, other Metro stations had remained open to minimise inconvenience to the travelling public,” the affidavit noted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks Delhi governmente to seek inputs from IB on Hawara plea for transfer to Punjab jail
stories.title: Supreme Court asks Delhi governmente to seek inputs from IB on Hawara plea for transfer to Punjab jail
stories.summary: Bench takes a cautious approach, saying the case of Beant Singh murder convict is sensitive, and even the Punjab government seems to be reluctant
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) asked the Delhi government to seek inputs from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Beant Singh murder convict Jagtar Singh Hawara’s plea for transfer from Delhi’s Tihar jail to a prison in Punjab.
A Bench headed by Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale took a cautious approach, saying the case was sensitive, and even the Punjab government seemed to be reluctant.
“We know that every sinner has a future… Like how somebody said, if you kill a single person, you are a murderer.
Kill a few thousand, you are a conqueror… But we will have to look at the implications of the transfer on the society,” Justice Sundresh said.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, informed the top court that Hawara was involved in a jailbreak and his death penalty was converted to life imprisonment in the murder case.
Contending that transfer might increase chances of his escape, Ms. Bhati referred to an advisory by the Ministry of Home Affairs on transfer of high-risk prisoners.
Senior advocate Colin Gonsalves, for Hawara, said he had personally visited his client in jail and found him completely reformed.
Ms. Bhati referred to a Punjab government affidavit which sounded apprehensive about the effect of Hawara’s shift on the law and order situation in the State.
Mr. Gonsalves submitted that the assassination of the Chief Minister happened in 1995 when his client was only 21 years old.
“His mother is very old, 82 years old and in serious condition.
He is only seeking a transfer to a Punjab high-security prison, and not seeking release.
He has a blemishless record in jail,” Mr. Gonsalves argued.

stories.title: Supreme Court probe panel to prioritise use of pellet gun, harassment of female protesters during July 20 march to Parliament
stories.summary: A statement by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said that for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel, the high-powered enquiry committee (HPEC) has launched a portal — http://hpec.nic.in
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court-appointed panel to investigate the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and places outside the national capital in July during the NEET paper leak protests will prioritise matters related to the “use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protesters, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side”.

A statement by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on behalf of the Supreme Court-constituted High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) said that for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel, the HPEC has launched a portal — http://hpec.nic.in.
“The HPEC shall examine all issues enumerated in paragraphs 12 and 13 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order dated 18 August 2026 and paragraph 5(i) of order dated 10 September, 2026.

Priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side,” the statement said.

The Hindu was the first to report on July 21 that at least one protester was hit by a pellet gun, part of the anti-riot gear of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) during the July 20 march to Parliament called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which turned violent.
Later, three more victims said they had been hit by pellets, usually fired from pump action guns.
Subsequently, on July 28, The Hindu reported that though Delhi.

Police denied the use of pellet guns, a general diary entry filed at Parliament Street police station revealed that the RAF fired two rounds from an anti-riot gun on the directions of a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)-rank officer of the police.

The demands for answers by the Opposition parties as to who ordered the use of pellet guns during the protests, in which at least 80 protesters were injured, and women were allegedly sexually assaulted by police personnel, led to the disruption of the monsoon session of Parliament.
The portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons.
The affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints/representations making use of the formats as applicable, it said.

“Apart from the above, any person wishing to provide information/suggestion relating to the issues referred to the HPEC under the orders dated 18 August 2026 and 10 September 2026 may also do so through the aforesaid portal.

stories.headline: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.title: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.summary: Chennai radar was indigenously renovated in 2022, and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is looking to strengthen its existing radar network alongside installing new radars to improve weather observations and track monsoons.
With the onset of Northeast monsoon on Thursday, the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre is maintaining the nearly 24-year-old Chennai’s-band doppler weather radar in working condition.
It is likely to be replaced with a new S-band radar by 2027.
Installed as India’s first doppler weather radar in 2002, Chennai’s radar on Rajaji Salai continues to monitor weather up to 400 km.
Officials of the RMC said orders have been placed to replace various radars, including Chennai, Karaikal, Kolkata and Machilipatnam about six months ago.
The supplier is awaiting a component from abroad before assembling the new equipment.
In 2022, Chennai radar was indigenously renovated and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection.
Four new S-Band and X-band radars would be installed at Kanniyakumari, Tiruchi, Yercaud and Ramanathapuram under the Mission Mausam.
Radars are being installed across the country in coordination with the respective State governments.
X band radars, which have a weather surveillance range of up to 180 km, would provide accurate observations of extreme weather events, said Sivananda Damodara Pai, Head, RMC.

Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD Director General, said besides the existing weather radars in places like Sriharikota, Pallikaranai, Karaikal and Chennai Rajaji Salai, new radars would cover more areas for weather observations.
Radars being maintained in the neighbouring States also help in Tamil Nadu’s weather surveillance.

stories.title: Govt. move to de-notify Jantar Mantar follows SC suggestion that protest sites need more space, open air
stories.summary: A four-page court order passed on October 9 records the Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant urging the government to look for a ‘spacious, open’ alternative site in Delhi
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: Exactly three days before the Delhi.

Police de-notified central Delhi’s Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site on Monday (October 12, 2026), the Supreme Court and the Union government were on the same page about finding an alternative site to “peacefully and lawfully” express dissent in the national capital.
On October 9, both the court and the government had reasoned that central Delhi was too cramped for protests.
It denied protesters basic amenities.
Observations and remarks were also exchanged about how inconvenient protests in and around Jantar Mantar were to ordinary commuters in Delhi.
The Chief Justice of India remarked that central Delhi did not have any washroom, medical and drinking water facilities.

The four-page order passed on October 9 actually records the Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant urging the Union government to look for a “spacious, open” alternative site.

The order was passed during the October 9 hearing on petitions challenging the government’s move to restrict access into and within the national capital, aimed at halting the October 10 youth protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
At the time of hearing, the protest was expected to happen at Jantar Mantar, the designated site for voicing dissent in the national capital.
The order said all the parties, including the petitioners, were in favour of finding an alternative protest site in Delhi.

“During the course of hearing, it was suggested, and counsel for the parties were ad idem (of the same mind), that it is high time basic amenities were provided to those engaged in peaceful and lawful protest.
